newsitem.title: PERU: Shell picks Intergen for Peru power plant.
newsitem.headline: Shell picks Intergen for Peru power plant.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group on Thursday said it selected International Generating Co (Intergen) to develop a proposal for a power plant fueled by natural gas from Peru's Camisea field.

U.S.-based Intergen beat out Community Energy Alternatives (CEA), which was also bidding to join Shell in developing what could be a single 300 megawatt (MW) generating plant, Shell said in a statement.

The plant "would supply power to the south of Peru where there is strong growth in electricity demand, primarily driven by demand from energy intensive industries such as the mining sector," the statement said.
The two U.S. companies originally formed a consortium to present a proposal, but they split up in February.

A 600 MW power plant to supply both the north and south of the country was originally under consideration, but lower-than-expected growth in demand in the north last year prompted the parties to consider a smaller plant, the statement said.
Last May, Royal Dutch/Shell and Mobil Corp signed a 40-year contract with the Peruvian government to explore and exploit the huge Camisea oil and gas reserves.
Shell, which is the operating partner in the project, estimates gas could be supplied to the power plant by the end of 1999.
